tina: Quick heads-up — ran a CI profile on the continuous-batcher for the last week. Observed long-sequence tenants consistently getting delayed behind high volume of short sequences. Token credits are being consumed by many tiny requests and KV cache churn seems to bias scheduling toward recently-hot short sequences. Attaching the lightweight profile below.

sam: Can you paste the p95 tail numbers and which model/config this hit? 7B quant only or wider? @tina

tina: Summary snippet from the profiler:```
tenant_type  avg_seq_len  kv_hit_rate  p95_latency_ms  queued_fraction
long_tenants  1024         0.72         890             0.42
short_tenants 24          0.56         120             0.18
mixed_pool    128         0.64         220             0.28
```
This was mostly on the 7B-quant path with our recent kernel-selection tweaks turned on. KV-hit_rate here is measured as prefix-KV hits within the same tenant window.

jordan: Hmm. Sounds like the batcher is prioritizing throughput for short requests which starves long ones because of token-budget accounting. Suggest we try a lane-weighting approach: short_lane for requests < 64 tokens with a strict tokens/sec cap, long_lane gets dynamic token budget that accrues while idle. Also consider a small bypass for tenants with high KV hotness to reduce cache churn.

alex: +1. For fairness I propose per-tenant soft credits (not hard limits) with replenishment: credits += min(max_credits, base_rate * delta_t + alpha * idle_seconds). If credits<threshold we route to long_lane with higher batch patience. Pseudocode:```
# credit update (runs every 50ms)
credits[tid] = min(max_credit, credits[tid] + base_rate*dt + alpha*idle)
if credits[tid] < long_threshold:
    enqueue(long_lane, req)
else:
    enqueue(short_lane, req)
```
This keeps short-path latency but gives long sequences time to accumulate tokens.

priya: I threw together a quick prototype queue policy `token_leaky_bucket` that implements the above and also factors in KV hit score (higher kv_hit gives slight priority bump). Config example:```
queue_policy: token_leaky_bucket
params:
  base_rate: 50   # tokens/sec default
  alpha: 0.2      # idle multiplier
  max_credit: 2000
  kv_bias: 0.1    # additive priority for kv-hit tenants
```
Will push to canary later today.

litao: Ran microbenchmarks (local canary) — paste results:```
Baseline (no lane weighting): long_tenant p50=610ms p95=920ms short_tenant p50=40ms p95=130ms
Prototype lane-weighting + kv_bias: long_tenant p50=420ms p95=600ms (huge win) short_tenant p50=45ms p95=140ms (slight regress)
Throughput: overall tokens/sec - static -2.1% ; short-path throughput -3.2%
```
Note: perf-regression-bot already flagged a small short-path throughput regression on commit abc123 (kernel-selection).

ops-bot: perf-regression-bot: Regression detected on commit abc123: short-sequence throughput -3% p50, triggered alert at 1718001500. See: https://perf/reports/abc123

maria: Good thread. Action items: (1) rollback the aggressive kernel-selection change for the short-path fallback (temp) to recover short throughput, (2) canary `token_leaky_bucket` lane-weighting at 10% traffic for next 48h with per-tenant soft credits, (3) add a KV-hit-aware batching heuristic that prefers grouping same-tenant prefixes when kv_hit_rate>0.7, (4) update the profiler dashboards to show credits and lane occupancy. @sam please own 1, @priya own 2+3, @litao handle dashboard changes and benchmark collection. :thumbsup:

sam: I can do 1, will create the rollback PR now.

priya: Starting canary rollout after the rollback is merged. Will add a short AB test and keep the short-path fallback as a fast-path escape hatch if p95 increases > 10%.

maria: Perfect — sync tomorrow after 24h canary. Thanks everyone. :)
